rows.condition: Every paper has a processing outcome; accepted mentions have evidence.
rows.note: Synthetic papers (a broken PDF, a named mention, a silent paper) each get an outcome from the fixed outcome set, and every extracted mention carries file hash, excerpt, location and review_status candidate_unreviewed. The pipeline accepts no mention by itself: reports/corpus_coverage.md (generated 2026-09-22) records 64 agent-complete mention inventories and 0 human-approved papers, so "accepted mentions have evidence" is checked only as "candidate mentions carry evidence"; human acceptance of mentions is not established by this row.

rows.condition: IDs survive sorting, pagination, remounting, and export/import.
rows.note: Sorting, cursor pagination and export/import of packs and saved selections are asserted in pytest on synthetic records. Remounting (returning to the same browsing state, re-importing a saved selection) is only covered by the Playwright specs, which this script checks exist but does not run; the re-import test there is skipped without ATLAS_LIVE_API.

rows.condition: Multiple questions reference one asset without duplicating image-only computation.
rows.note: Asset-unit queries collapse shared images; the detector runs once for byte-identical originals; run estimates count unique assets; the asset worker batches a repeated asset once. Synthetic fixtures only; no real multi-question dataset is exercised by these nodes.

rows.condition: Join failures are counted and visible; no silent record loss.
rows.note: attach_results (the pack overlay join) now counts a result item whose record is absent as coverage.items_unjoined on the attached artifact; the Parquet join and the publication overlay reject such an item loudly. Automated checks only.

rows.condition: Static and workbench providers return the same IDs for supported queries over the same snapshot.
rows.note: pytest compares the pack query path with the Parquet workbench path on the same synthetic snapshot (filter, sort, sampling, paging). The TypeScript static provider is compared with Python-generated cases by Vitest (apps/web/src/query.test.ts against apps/web/src/test-fixtures/query-parity.json, produced by apps/web/scripts/generate_query_parity_fixture.py); `npm test` is not run by this script, so that half is not re-verified here.

rows.condition: Preview-only results never appear as complete-release statistics.
rows.note: Query results and aggregates carry population_scope and a preview warning, and a preview pack refuses a complete-scope request. Whether the interface always shows that label is asserted only in the Playwright spec, which is not run here.

rows.condition: Saved IDs reproduce the selection; unit and method remain visible.
rows.note: Seeded samples are reproducible and portable between providers; saved selections store the actual IDs, unit and query and survive export. Method and unit appear in query results (coverage.sampling, unit); how the interface renders them is not asserted by these nodes.

rows.condition: Filtered search respects its population; exact results validate approximate indexes.

not_applicable_clauses.cite: SPEC 11.3 and 11.4 (approximate indexes are added only after measuring workload; exact search is the validation path once they exist)

rows.note: Retrieval is exact LanceDB search prefiltered to the eligible identities (SPEC 11.3). The clause about validating approximate indexes is not_applicable: a grep of src/ finds no index creation, IVF, HNSW or FAISS use, and the search bypasses the vector index; the cited node re-checks that claim. If an approximate index is ever added, this clause becomes applicable and needs a recall-against-exact test (SPEC 11.4). The LanceDB-backed nodes are skipped where lancedb is not installed; a skip is not a pass.

rows.condition: Missing, failed, and zero-detection cases remain distinct.
rows.note: Zero detections count as 0, failed items keep no output, absent records are not_applicable, and a partially failed record reports null counts rather than 0. The display of missing/failed/zero states is in the Playwright spec and its recorded receipt, not re-run here.

rows.condition: Overlays align after orientation, resizing, and letterboxing transformations.
rows.note: pytest checks EXIF-transposed dimensions and box clamping to the transposed image. Pixel alignment through browser resizing and object-fit letterboxing is asserted only by the Playwright spec (an EXIF-6 fixture, 1 CSS pixel tolerance); it is not run by this script, so that evidence rests on the receipt in reports/browser-verification.md.

rows.condition: Recolouring/filtering does not refit; artifact provenance survives export.
rows.note: pytest: a fit has a stable fit_id and fitted-ID set, a result join and filter leave the artifact unchanged, and processor provenance survives pack export/import. Recolouring in the browser not refitting is shown only by the runtime journey receipt (projection_sha256_unchanged) and its Playwright spec, which are not re-run here.

rows.condition: Text-only models receive no false image-access claim; evaluation excludes disallowed fields.
rows.note: Against a mock transport: a text-only evaluation context states that images are unavailable, excludes gold labels, filenames and model answers, refuses hidden fields, and needs a verified image capability and real bytes before any image is sent. No real model is called by these nodes.

rows.condition: Bounds, schemas, roots, and network restrictions are enforced outside the model.
rows.note: Allowlist, row limit, record scope, call budget, wall-clock deadline, configured media roots with symlink rejection, HTTPS-only external endpoints and a fail-closed external-transmission policy are asserted in code outside the model, with mock providers.

rows.condition: Cancellation and restart do not duplicate successful work or register corrupt artifacts.
rows.note: Successful items are not recomputed after restart, cancelled runs keep partial results and resume, a foreign or oversized staged result is rejected, and a tampered run import registers nothing. Analysis jobs use synthetic records; preparation retry is checked at the plan/receipt level.

rows.condition: Secrets, absolute paths, PDFs, and unapproved media are rejected.
rows.note: Synthetic records with a bearer token, a local absolute path or a PDF reference are refused before anything is written; unapproved media and annotations are stripped, and disguised media fails its checksum. The receipts record the real publication validation (three approved previews) and archive inspection as of 2026-10-07; they are not regenerated here.

rows.condition: Browser-only use does not require GPU/model dependencies.
rows.note: The base dependency list names no model package and importing the API and CLI loads none. The receipts record fresh base-only virtual environments on Python 3.12 and 3.14 serving the bundled interface and approved previews over real HTTP with optional_model_packages_present empty. reports/installation-verification.json and its python314 twin certify an earlier wheel (sha256 b3b00fc4...); the current wheel (sha256 74656ccf..., named in reports/final-status.json) is covered by the two installation-factoid-current receipts. A rebuilt wheel needs new receipts. These receipts do not certify any optional model package (torch, transformers, nudenet, lancedb, scikit-learn, umap): they show only that such packages are not needed for browser use.
